Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you make this into a clear prompt for a short handoff note, not write the note yet. it's for our small theatre lighting crew, we're doing thursday afternoon cue-to-cue in the studio. the overhead led wash is on dimmer channel 14, and after about ten minutes it started flickering. at the next test we need two separate paths, and the note should make it really clear which one applies. if channel 14 is still flickering then don't swap out the fixture; isolate channel 14 at the dimmer rack, write “hold for electrician” on the patch sheet, and tell the stage manager that the channel is unavailable. but if it isn't flickering during that next test, leave both the fixture and the patch as they are and carry on with the planned cue check. don't make it sound like we've decided which result we'll get, since the test hasn't happened yet. the note is for the board operator and electrician to see at the end of rehearsal, so use plain, direct wording and don't add a technical diagnosis. just organize that into a usable request for generating the handoff note, with the condition and the other option easy to follow.", "output": "Write a short, plain-language handoff note for the small theatre lighting crew about the overhead LED wash during Thursday afternoon’s cue-to-cue rehearsal in the studio. The wash is on dimmer channel 14 and began flickering after about ten minutes. The next test has not happened yet, so do not assume its result. Clearly distinguish these two actions:

- If channel 14 is still flickering during the next test, do not swap out the fixture. Isolate channel 14 at the dimmer rack, write “hold for electrician” on the patch sheet, and tell the stage manager that the channel is unavailable.
- If channel 14 is not flickering during the next test, leave the fixture and patch unchanged and continue with the planned cue check.

Use direct wording suitable for the board operator and electrician to read at the end of rehearsal. Do not add a technical diagnosis."}]
